title: Normal charts and regular boundary equation on a full SNC root limit
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, $k$ a field of characteristic $p$, $Y$ a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], and $B=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ an affine etale chart. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$, $r\geq0$, be branch equations of a reduced strict normal crossings divisor on $B$, whose branches are precisely $V(t_d)$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $A\to R$ be weakly etale, meaning that this ring map and $R\otimes_A R\to R$ are flat [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Write
$$S=\varinjlim_{n\geq1,\ (n,p)=1}R[x_{1,n},\ldots,x_{r,n}]/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_{1\leq d\leq r},$$
with transition $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$, using polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and ring colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every weakly etale $S$-algebra $Q$, the ring $Q$ is normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: each prime localization $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. Moreover multiplication by the image $s\in Q$ of $t_1\cdots t_r$ is injective on $Q$. The zero algebra $Q$ and empty chart are allowed. For $r=0$, the product is $1$ and $S=R$.

source.place: Agent geometric extension of Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, printed p.133 (finite simultaneous parameter-root normal form). Infinite and weakly etale extension uses Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 2.3.4, Stacks Tag 037D (algebra-lemma-colimit-normal-ring), and normality descent. WANTED: an exact reference for this combined infinite-chart formulation.

proof.text: Write $A_n=A[x_{1,n},\ldots,x_{r,n}]/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d$. The SNC hypothesis includes regularity of $B$ (take the empty subset in the boundary definition). Since $(n,p)=1$, Bezout gives an inverse of $n\cdot1_A$ in the characteristic-$p$ algebra $A$. Apply [lem-sfb-snc-finite-root-regular-ring] to this regular affine SNC pair: every $A_n$ is a regular Noetherian ring. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal] makes every $A_n$ normal. This assertion concerns the finite algebras over $A$, before weakly etale base change.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 proof, p.133; Stacks Tag 0567 (algebra-lemma-regular-normal).

proof.text: Put $R_n=R[x_{1,n},\ldots,x_{r,n}]/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d$. The tensor pushout universal property identifies $A_n\otimes_A R$ with $R_n$: send $x_{d,n}\otimes1$ to the displayed root and $1\otimes a$ to $a\in R$; conversely send each coefficient $a\in R$ to $1\otimes a$ and each root to $x_{d,n}\otimes1$. The root relations hold in both rings, and the composites fix all coefficients and roots. Thus $A_n\to R_n$ is the base change of $A\to R$ and is weakly etale by [lem-exc-weakly-etale-ring-base-change-composition].

For each $n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-existing-weakly-etale-indetale-refinement] to $A_n\to R_n$. Obtain a faithfully flat $R_n\to T_n$ with $A_n\to T_n$ ind-etale. By the definition of ind-etale, $T_n$ is a small filtered colimit of finitely presented etale $A_n$-algebras. Every such algebra is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal], since Step 1 proved $A_n$ normal. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring] makes $T_n$ normal. Faithfully flat descent [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-normal-ring-descent] now makes $R_n$ normal. The refinement and descent statements impose no Noetherian condition on $R_n$ or $T_n$.

The positive integers prime to $p$, ordered by divisibility, form a small nonempty directed poset: $1$ belongs to it, and $nm$ is an upper bound for $n,m$ and remains prime to $p$. The prescribed transition respects each relation because $(x_{d,m}^{m/n})^n=t_d$, and transitions compose because $(m/n)(l/m)=l/n$. Thus the displayed $S$ is the filtered colimit of the normal rings $R_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring] to conclude that $S$ is normal; no injectivity assumption on its transitions is needed.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-existing-weakly-etale-indetale-refinement] to the given weakly etale map $S\to Q$. It supplies a faithfully flat map $Q\to H$ for which $S\to H$ is ind-etale. Its filtered etale presentation has normal terms by Step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal]. Hence $H$ is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring], and $Q$ is normal by [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-normal-ring-descent]. This is normality in the prime-localization sense stated in the item, including rings which are not domains.

For injectivity start on $A$. By Step 1 with $n=1$ (where $A_1=A$), $A$ is a regular Noetherian ring, so each $A_{\mathfrak m}$ at a maximal ideal is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], hence a domain [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. Fix $d$ and $y\in A$ with $t_dy=0$. In $A_{\mathfrak m}$ either $y/1=0$ or $t_d/1=0$. In the latter case let $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be the preimage of the prime $(0)\subset A_{\mathfrak m}$; then $A_{\mathfrak q}=\operatorname{Frac}(A_{\mathfrak m})$ is a field, of dimension $0$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and $t_d\in\mathfrak q$, so $\mathfrak q\in V(t_d)=C_d$. The SNC definition with $J=\{d\}$ at $z=\mathfrak q$ gives $\dim A_{\mathfrak q}=\dim(A/t_dA)_{\mathfrak q}+1\geq1$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], since $(A/t_dA)_{\mathfrak q}\neq0$. This contradiction shows $y/1=0$ in every $A_{\mathfrak m}$, so $y=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-membership-at-maximal-localizations] with $J=0$. Composing these injective multiplications gives injectivity of $s_A=\prod_dt_d$ on $A$; the empty composite is the identity, and $A=0$ is trivial.

source.place: Tag 00NP (lemma-regular-domain) and Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local); the codimension clause of the SNC definition (ILO VIII 4.1.2, Stacks etale.tex Tag 0BI9).

proof.text: The weakly etale map $A\to R$ is flat. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], tensoring the injection $A\xrightarrow{s_A}A$ with $R$ gives injectivity of multiplication by $s_R$ on $R$ (identify $A\otimes_A R$ with $R$ by $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$). Repeatedly apply [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] to the $r$ monic equations $X^n-t_d$: $R_n$ is free over $R$ on the monomials $\prod_d x_{d,n}^{a_d}$ with $0\leq a_d<n$. If $s_Rv=0$ in $R_n$, uniqueness of this expansion gives $s_Rc_a=0$ for each coefficient, hence $c_a=0$ and $v=0$. Thus multiplication by $s$ is injective at every finite stage.

source.place: Tag 00HB (definition-flat); monic polynomial division, as in Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), proof of (10) implies (1).

proof.text: Let $v\in S$ satisfy $sv=0$. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], choose $n$ and $v_n\in R_n$ representing $v$. The equality of the images of $s v_n$ and $0$ holds at a common later stage $m$ by the same elementwise theorem. The image $v_m$ therefore satisfies $s v_m=0$ in $R_m$. Step 7 forces $v_m=0$, so $v=0$ in $S$. Finally $S\to Q$ is flat by the definition of weakly etale. Tensor the injection $S\xrightarrow{s}S$ with $Q$ using [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The resulting map is multiplication by the specified image of $s$ on $Q$, so it is injective.

source.place: Filtered ring-colimit representatives and eventual equality (Tag 002W via algebraic filtered colimits); Tag 00HB (definition-flat).

proof.text: If the chart or $Q$ is empty, its ring is zero; injectivity on its one-element underlying set holds, and the local normality condition has no primes to check. If $r=0$, every finite root algebra is its base ring, all power transitions are identities, $S=R$, and $s=1$. Steps 3 and 5 still prove normality, and multiplication by $1$ is the identity. The same proof also includes $n=1$.
